issues.where: example/An angular character on the Gaussian integers
issues.problem: Claimed the Dirichlet coefficients of L(s, xi_4) lie 'on or inside the unit circle'. False: a coefficient is a sum over all ideals of norm n; at the split prime 313 it is about -1.97. Also 'complex numbers' is misleading: the coefficients are real because conjugate ideals give conjugate values.
issues.fix: Rewrote the closing remark: coefficients are real, not integers, can exceed 1 in size (313 example); infinite order seen from (-7+24i)/25 not being a root of unity. Added exact-arithmetic check (also of the n=25 coefficient -429/625).

issues.problem: A check's claim text said '{1,2,5,7} is not Sidon mod 5' while the code (and the lesson) use mod 8; Singer's theorem beyond q=2,3 and the Baker-Harman-Pintz lower bound sqrt N - O(N^0.2625) were unchecked.
issues.fix: Corrected the claim text; added a check finding perfect difference sets for q=4,5 and testing q+1 >= sqrt N - N^0.2625 for sampled N up to 10^9.
